newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilians less upbeat on Real economic plan -poll.
newsitem.headline: Brazilians less upbeat on Real economic plan -poll.

text.p: Brazilians are less optimistic about the success of the government's Real anti-inflation plan and growing numbers fear unemployment and plan to reduce spending in the coming months, a poll released Tuesday said.

The survey by the National Industry Confederation (CNI) and private pollster IBOPE said the percentage who feel the three-year-old stabilization plan has been a success fell to 36 percent in May from 46 percent in March.
The poll, which surveyed the opinions of 2,000 people across Brazil from May 7-13, added that 40 percent feel it is still too early to draw conclusions on the Real Plan.

The CNI/IBOPE survey, which did not give a margin of error, also revealed those who feel their life has improved since the plan went into effect in June 1994 dropped to 47 percent in May from 55 percent in March.
The poll said 69 percent feared losing their jobs, the highest since polling began in February 1996 and up from 60 percent in the last two CNI/IBOPE surveys in March 1997 and November 1996.

It added those planning to buy less over the next three months rose to 27 percent versus 26 percent a year ago, and 28 percent are more indebted than they were three months ago, the highest level since the polling began in February 1996.
"The intentions of buying have evolved in step with indebtedness, diminishing when the later rises and vice versa," a CNI statement outlining the results of the poll said.
The survey showed Brazilians feel that recession, unemployment, rising public service prices and high interest rates pose the greatest threats to the economic program.
Despite the darkening public mood regarding the Real Plan, Brazilian industry remains upbeat on the future of the economy, CNI president Sen. Fernando Bezerra was quoted as saying.

"Our expectations for the future are optimistic," Bezerra said in the statement. "We think it is necessary to complete the picture in the country with the adoption of reforms, deregulation of monopolies and acceleration of privatizations."
He said those steps would solidify the economy's stabilization and lead to growth in productivity and more jobs.
